summary: Durable L1 environment-layer store (exec-plane S3 A2/A3, cinatra#1708; epic #1705). Two brand-new tables backing the injectable EnvironmentLayerStore so the exec-plane EnvironmentLayerCache is CROSS-PROCESS (a later process reuses an earlier build; the retention GC and lifecycle reference-drop share one durable source of truth — the precondition for the S3 GC/teardown criteria AC1 reuse, AC3/AC6 lifecycle): (1) environment_layers — content-addressed L1 cache entries, UNIQUE (recipe_key, partition) via environment_layers_recipe_partition_uniq (partition NOT NULL, 'instance' sentinel — one recipe may exist as an instance-shared layer AND one-or-more org-partitioned layers; one org's UPSERT never clobbers another's); (2) environment_layer_references — org-scoped recipe->layer references, UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (recipe_key, org_id, holder_package_name, holder_template_id, holder_version_id) via environment_layer_references_dedup_uniq (nullable holder columns for packaged vs project agents; PG15+ NULLS NOT DISTINCT reproduces the in-memory addReference dedup). NO foreign keys ON PURPOSE (artifact_uninstall_operations / dispatch-ledger precedent): durable references outlive the referencing install rows; recipe/holder ids validated at WRITE time, not FK-enforced at rest. ADDITIVE (two brand-new empty tables + their indexes; no row rejected, no data rewrite) — no artifact is REQUIRED; shipped anyway (core__0037/0047/0055 precedent) to keep the fresh-bootstrap and operator-upgrade paths in lockstep with the idempotent buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries mirror (environmentLayerStoreSchemaQueries). down() drops both tables and their indexes (the durable cache/reference rows are non-recoverable operational state; they regenerate on the next build/reference). SEQ IS PROVISIONAL: assigned at merge — shipped max on origin/main at build time is core__0056; a concurrent lane may claim 0057 first, in which case renumber-at-merge is normal. migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
